products.name: Metabase
products.description: Open-source BI platform enabling self-service analytics with visual query builder, SQL editor, and embeddable dashboards. Targets SMBs and startups with ease-of-use focus.
products.positioning: Accessible, open-source BI for data teams who want exploration without vendor lock-in

products.name: Apache Superset
products.description: Apache-licensed open-source data visualization and BI platform. Supports 35+ data sources with intuitive interface for non-technical users. Emphasis on composable analytics and semantic layers.
products.positioning: Enterprise-grade, open-source BI with strong data integration and no vendor lock-in

products.name: Tableau
products.description: Enterprise BI platform renowned for sophisticated interactive dashboards and visualization flexibility. 2026 releases add Tableau Agent for conversational analytics, Dynamic Zone Visibility for personalization, and Pace to Goal insights.
products.positioning: Premium visualization gold standard with advanced analytics and AI-assisted authoring for large enterprises

products.name: Microsoft Power BI
products.description: Microsoft's cloud-native BI platform integrated with Excel, Azure, and Microsoft 365. Copilot-enabled for AI-assisted authoring in 2026. Focus on cost-effectiveness, Microsoft ecosystem integration, and natural language queries.
products.positioning: AI-first, Microsoft-ecosystem BI with best price-to-performance ratio for enterprises

products.name: Google Looker
products.description: Google Cloud's enterprise BI platform centered on data governance and metric consistency. LookML code-based modeling ensures consistent definitions. 2026 adds Dashboard Agents with conversational AI, in-database analytics, and Looker-managed MCP servers.
products.positioning: Data governance-first BI for large enterprises requiring single source of truth and engineering rigor

products.name: Grafana
products.description: Open-source monitoring and observability platform with time-series data focus. Grafana Labs (Series E, $6B valuation, Sequoia-backed) offers cloud hosting and enterprise features. 2026 adds Grafana Assistant AI, dynamic dashboards, and Git Sync GA.
products.positioning: Operational monitoring and observability leader with AI-assisted analysis for DevOps/SRE teams

products.name: Redash
products.description: Open-source SQL-first querying and visualization platform supporting 35+ data sources. Emphasizes ease of use for SQL-native analysts. Connects directly to databases and data warehouses with scheduled queries and alerts.
products.positioning: SQL-first, lightweight BI for technical teams and data engineers

products.name: Amazon QuickSight
products.description: AWS-native BI platform with per-session reader pricing ($3/month). 2026 releases add 22 new APIs for Spaces/Agents/Flows, BI migration agents, Generative BI, and ML insights. Tight AWS ecosystem integration with S3, RDS, Redshift, Athena.
products.positioning: AWS-native BI with emerging agent/flow capabilities and cost-effective reader model for broad consumption

products.name: Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition (OBIEE)
products.description: Legacy enterprise BI platform being transitioned to Oracle Analytics Server/Cloud. Extended support ending Dec 2025. Historically strong in enterprises with Oracle databases but complex to deploy and maintain.
products.positioning: Legacy enterprise BI for Oracle-centric organizations (in transition to OAS/OAC)

they_win_on: Open-source with no vendor lock-in; lower total cost of ownership for self-hosted deployments
Simple, intuitive UI optimized for SMBs and startups who prioritize ease-of-use over advanced features
Lightweight, fast to deploy (Docker, JAR) with minimal infrastructure overhead
we_win_on: Graph-native workflow visualization (Metabase is dashboard-only, no node/edge representation for processes)
AI + UI parity: conversational interface paired with visible graph structure prevents 'flight to chat'
Semantic layer enforcement: MetroGraph enforces graph-based metric definitions with visualization, while Metabase relies on UI-based models with less transparency
competitors.wedge_vs_them: Position as Metabase for workflow/data pipeline teams: same ease-of-use, but add the graph layer to see queries/transforms/joins as nodes, run them interactively, and trace lineage—eliminating the 'dashboard guessing game' when data changes.
competitors.moat: Open-source and self-hosted (free tier); community contributions; embedded SDK for startups

they_win_on: Open-source Apache project with 73K GitHub stars; strong community trust and contribution velocity
Better data integration story: 35+ connectors, MongoDB support, OAuth2 overhaul (2026) show data pipeline integration focus
Composable analytics emphasis aligns with dbt/modern data stack ethos (Preset as managed option adds support)
we_win_on: Graph visualization for data lineage and workflow dependencies (Superset treats lineage as metadata, not a first-class UI element)
Semantic layer that's queryable and traversable as a graph (vs Superset's metadata-driven approach)
Prevents surface-area bloat by enforcing graph-based navigation instead of endless dashboards
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For data engineers who use Superset today: add MetroGraph as the 'workflow layer' above dashboards. Use the graph to model data transformations and their dependencies; query it conversationally; Superset provides the final-stage BI. Reduces Superset 'dashboard sprawl' by centralizing flow logic.
competitors.moat: Apache licensing, community governance, integrations with dbt/modern data stack

they_win_on: Unmatched visualization and interactivity: 30+ chart types with pixel-perfect control; Hyper engine handles massive datasets efficiently
Gold standard in enterprise visualization: Tableau Agent (2026) adds conversational analytics without losing visual sophistication
Established ecosystem: 100+ connectors, strong community, industry benchmark for data storytelling
we_win_on: Graph-first interaction model: Tableau embeds agent as a sidebar; MetroGraph makes the graph the primary canvas with optional chat, reducing confusion between 'ask chart' and 'ask data'
Semantic layer as graphs: Tableau's 2026 Semantic Models are UI-configured; MetroGraph's semantic layer is queryable/traversable as a node/edge network
HCI for complex workflows: Tableau is dashboard-composition tool; MetroGraph is orchestration/lineage-visualization tool—prevents sprawl when users have 500+ metrics
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For Fortune 500 analytics teams managing complex metrics/lineage: MetroGraph sits upstream of Tableau. Use the graph to govern metric definitions and data dependencies; push validated metrics to Tableau for final visualization. Tableau + MetroGraph = separation of concerns (flow orchestration vs. visual storytelling).
competitors.moat: Visualization leadership, enterprise mindshare, Hyper performance, broad connector ecosystem, acquisition by Salesforce

they_win_on: Copilot integration (2026): highest GenAI functionality score per Forrester; natural language dashboards; most affordable enterprise BI at $14/user/mo
Microsoft ecosystem lock-in: Excel, Azure, Dynamics, M365 users have frictionless onboarding; 400+ connectors
AI-first positioning attracts CISO/CIO buyers worried about GenAI parity with Tableau
we_win_on: AI + UI parity problem: Power BI's Copilot is a chat sidebar; users flip between 'ask Copilot' and 'use dashboard'; MetroGraph keeps graph visible throughout, preventing disorientation
DAX complexity: Power BI's semantic model requires DAX mastery; MetroGraph's node/edge model is more intuitive for non-data-scientists
Metric governance: Power BI's DAX-based semantic model is less transparent than MetroGraph's graph visualization of metric dependencies
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For Microsoft shops frustrated with DAX and Copilot chat isolation: MetroGraph as the 'Copilot layer' that works with Power BI. Use MetroGraph's conversational graph interface to explore metrics, then push to Power BI for visualization. DAX logic becomes visible as graph nodes.
competitors.moat: Microsoft ecosystem integration, Copilot AI, aggressive pricing, installed base (M365 users)

they_win_on: Data governance moat: LookML enforces metric consistency via code; single source of truth unmatched in industry; 2026 Dashboard Agents add conversational analytics without sacrificing governance
BigQuery integration: native semantic layer, in-database analytics, Looker-managed MCP servers (2026); tight Google Cloud alignment
Engineering rigor: Git-native workflow, version control, code review, team collaboration—appeals to data-engineering teams
we_win_on: LookML is code-based but not visual: MetroGraph's node/edge model makes dependencies and transformations visible without requiring LookML literacy
Accessibility: Looker's semantic layer requires engineering mindset; MetroGraph democratizes flow visualization for BI analysts who code occasionally
Agent + Graph synergy: Looker's Dashboard Agents are BI-scoped; MetroGraph agents traverse the entire data graph (metrics → tables → joins), not just dashboard-level questions
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For Google Cloud + Looker shops: MetroGraph as the 'before LookML' layer. Visually design your metric graph, auto-generate LookML, push to Looker. Reduces LookML rework when metric definitions change.
competitors.moat: LookML semantic layer, BigQuery integration, Google Cloud momentum, engineering credibility

they_win_on: Time-series and observability focus: Grafana is the category leader for DevOps/SRE monitoring; 1000+ plugins for extensibility; Series E funding ($6B) signals momentum
Alerting and notifications: unified alerting engine with multi-channel support (Slack, PagerDuty, email); superior to BI platforms for operational monitoring
Open-source + enterprise: free tier with cloud option; good freemium model for SMBs
we_win_on: Business analytics vs operations: Grafana optimizes for time-series dashboards; MetroGraph optimizes for metric definition and lineage traversal
Graph semantics: Grafana's plugin ecosystem is extensible but lacks semantic layer; MetroGraph enforces consistent metric definitions across the graph
Non-observability use cases: Grafana is DevOps-centric; MetroGraph targets data engineers and BI analysts with broader analytics scope
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For DevOps teams running Grafana: MetroGraph as the 'data pipeline governance layer' feeding Grafana alerts. Use MetroGraph to model and validate metric flows before alerting rules consume them.
competitors.moat: Time-series optimization, plugin ecosystem, observability credibility, Sequoia/Lightspeed backing

they_win_on: SQL-first philosophy: Redash's core strength is query-focused BI for data engineers; excellent SQL editor and parameter support
Lightweight deployment: minimal overhead, fast to deploy, good for SMBs and startups
Open-source with managed option: good freemium model; community-driven development
we_win_on: Beyond SQL: Redash excels at querying individual data sources; MetroGraph adds orchestration and lineage—seeing how queries chain together
Semantic layer: Redash has no semantic layer; MetroGraph enforces metric definitions and makes them navigable
Scaling to complexity: Redash works well for 10-100 queries; MetroGraph handles 1000+ metrics with graph-based governance
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For Redash users managing growing metric complexity: MetroGraph as the 'Redash organizer'. Use MetroGraph to model query dependencies and metric relationships; output queries to Redash for visualization.
competitors.moat: SQL-first positioning, ease of use for analysts, open-source credibility

they_win_on: AWS-native and cost-effective: SPICE in-memory, reader pricing ($3/mo) enables broad consumption; 22 new APIs (2026) for Agents/Flows signal emerging agentic platform

Emerging agent capabilities: BI migration agents (2026), generative BI; Amazon is investing in agentic BI
we_win_on: Workflow orchestration: QuickSight's agents are BI-focused (answering questions); MetroGraph agents traverse the data graph (understanding lineage, dependencies, transformations)
Graph visualization: QuickSight is dashboard-first; MetroGraph is graph-first (nodes = tables/metrics, edges = relationships)
Semantic layer maturity: QuickSight's semantic model is emerging; MetroGraph's is graph-based and queryable
competitors.wedge_vs_them: For AWS shops using QuickSight: MetroGraph as the 'query orchestration layer' on top. Use MetroGraph to model data pipelines and metric definitions; QuickSight handles visualization.
competitors.moat: AWS ecosystem integration, cost-effective reader model, emerging agentic features, AWS sales force

they_win_on: Legacy enterprise mindshare: entrenched in Fortune 500 organizations with Oracle DB; strong for large organizations with existing Oracle infrastructure
Deep Oracle integration: native to Oracle Database, Exadata; strong in regulated industries (finance, healthcare)
we_win_on: Modern architecture: OBIEE is legacy monolith; MetroGraph is cloud-native, API-first, composable
Developer experience: OBIEE's XML/BI Beans model is ancient; MetroGraph's graph-based UI is contemporary
Ease of deployment: OBIEE is on-premise complexity; MetroGraph is cloud/Docker simplicity
AI/ML: OBIEE has no AI assistant; MetroGraph is conversational from day one
